items.q: Why does Mark treat the first $10,000 as special?
items.a: It is the **hardest and most important** milestone — proof that making money is a **skill, not luck**. Once you make **10K once**, you know you can repeat and scale into wealth.

items.q: Should beginners use crypto or day trading as primary income?
items.a: No. Those need **capital and luck**. Treat them as **multipliers**, not the engine that earns the first lump sum from zero.

items.q: Which side-hustle category wins if speed is the goal?
items.a: **Online services** (copywriting, video editing, thumbnails, ads, social). They combine **global reach** with **70–80% margins** and **cash from day one**, unlike local products' thin margins or dropshipping's 1–3 month ramp.

items.q: How do you pick a service without overthinking?
items.a: Ask: What are you **good at**? What do you **enjoy learning**? What problems do **businesses always struggle with**? Start **under market rate** to earn and learn — don't wait months to "perfect" skills first.

items.q: What four pyramid elements keep freelancers stuck if missing?
items.a: **Positioning**, **leverage**, **reach**, and **automation/reliability**. Miss one and income stalls even if you're talented.

items.q: How should you position and price as a student freelancer?
items.a: Sell to **businesses**, not individuals — a shop doing **$50K/month** will pay **$2K** for outcomes. Charge for **ROI, not hours**, and use content (TikTok portfolio) so clients **inbound** instead of only cold pitching.

items.q: What underrated moat beats raw talent?
items.a: **Reliability**. Mark says **95% of freelancers miss deadlines** despite talent; clients pay thousands to the **organized** (CRM, pipeline, follow-ups), not always the best.

items.q: What should you do with earnings until ~$1M?
items.a: Avoid **lifestyle inflation**. The wealthy **reinvest**; the rich spend. Climb safest → riskiest: **high-interest savings (~3%)** → **index funds/ETFs** → individual stocks → crypto via DCA.

items.q: What's the coffee-to-million math Mark uses for index funds?
items.a: Redirecting about **$5/day coffee** into broad indexes (S&P ~**10%** avg last decade; VTSAX / VWRL etc.) compounds toward **$1M by 67** in his illustrative math — not financial advice.
